bands.title: Lower self-esteem right now
bands.summary: Your answers suggest you are currently quite hard on yourself and may find it difficult to see your own worth. This is common, and self-esteem can grow with time and support.

bands.title: Moderate self-esteem
bands.summary: Your answers suggest a generally balanced view of yourself, with some areas where self-doubt shows up.

bands.title: Healthy self-esteem
bands.summary: Your answers suggest you generally value and accept yourself, while still seeing room to grow.

support.text: If feelings of worthlessness are persistent or overwhelming, talking with a counsellor or someone you trust can really help. You deserve support.

worth.low: You may sometimes doubt that you matter or deserve good things.
worth.moderate: You generally see your value, though it may waver at times.
worth.high: You have a steady sense that you matter and deserve respect.
worth.reflect: What would you say to a friend who felt the way you do about yourself?
worth.tip: Each evening, write down one thing you did that reflects who you want to be.

acceptance.low: You may be critical of your flaws and sometimes wish you were different.
acceptance.moderate: You accept much of who you are, with some parts you still struggle with.
acceptance.high: You are comfortable with who you are, imperfections included.
acceptance.reflect: Which part of yourself is hardest to accept, and why?
acceptance.tip: When you notice a flaw, try adding "and that's human" to the thought.

respect.low: You may put others' needs before your own, even when it costs you.
respect.moderate: You often honour your own needs, though boundaries can slip under pressure.
respect.high: You protect your needs and set boundaries when you need to.
respect.reflect: Where in your life would a clearer boundary help you?
respect.tip: Practise one small "no" this week to something that drains you.

confidence.low: You may doubt your judgement and avoid challenges for fear of failing.
confidence.moderate: You trust yourself in familiar areas, with more doubt in new situations.
confidence.high: You trust your abilities and are willing to take on challenges.
confidence.reflect: What is one challenge you avoided recently, and what would trying it look like?
confidence.tip: Set a small, achievable goal and notice the confidence that comes from finishing it.

perception.low: You may struggle to recognise your strengths and often compare yourself unfavourably with others.
perception.moderate: You see some of your strengths, though comparison can cloud the picture.
perception.high: You recognise your good qualities and what you are good at.
perception.reflect: What strengths would the people closest to you say you have?
perception.tip: Ask someone you trust what they value about you, and write it down.

selftalk.low: Your inner voice may be harsh, especially after mistakes.
selftalk.moderate: Your inner voice is sometimes kind and sometimes critical.
selftalk.high: You tend to speak to yourself with encouragement and understanding.
selftalk.reflect: What do you usually say to yourself after a mistake?
selftalk.tip: Next time you make a mistake, respond to yourself as you would to a good friend.

suggestions: Self-esteem changes over time. This is a snapshot, not a verdict.
Small, kind habits, like noticing what went well each day, can gradually shift how you see yourself.
If low self-worth weighs on you, a counsellor can help you explore it safely.
note: Your score is the average of all 25 answers (negatively worded questions flipped), shown on a 0–100 scale. It combines the 10 Rosenberg questions with 15 MindCheck questions, so it is not an official Rosenberg score.
